prompt: What is a cache stampede?
hint: The moment a popular key expires.

choices.text: Many misses on one key
Redis running out of memory
Two writers racing
A cache that never expires anything

prompt: Fifty readers at once missed book 2 through `bookcache`. How many database queries did they cause?
A page is read 500 times a second and its query takes 120 ms. About how many identical queries reach the database when its key expires?
Why can a stampede get worse once it starts?

choices.text: Redis slows down under load and drops keys
choices.why: The database is the one under load.

choices.text: The window widens as the database slows
Each miss deletes another key
The lifetime of the key gets shorter

prompt: Why does the lock in `lockcache.py` have `px=LOCK_MS`?

choices.text: To make the lock faster to take
So a crashed holder blocks nobody forever
Redis requires a lifetime on every key
To keep the copy fresh for that long
choices.why: That is the TTL of the copy.

prompt: What goes wrong if a reader releases the lock with a plain `DEL`, without the token?
hint: A reader slower than the lock's lifetime.

choices.text: Nothing; DEL is atomic
choices.why: Atomic, and still the wrong lock.

choices.text: Redis refuses to delete a key with NX
It deletes another reader's lock
The cached copy is deleted as well

prompt: With a crashed reader's lock left behind for 2,000 ms, roughly how long did the fifty readers take, in milliseconds?
hint: The lock's lifetime, plus one query.

prompt: In `swrcache.py`, why does the key live an hour longer than the copy is fresh?
hint: Something must be there to serve.

choices.text: So there is a stale copy to serve
Redis rounds lifetimes up to the hour
To save memory
So that the refresh flag lasts that long too

prompt: Where is serving stale the wrong choice?
hint: An old answer must be acceptable.

choices.text: A book's description
choices.why: A few seconds old is fine.

choices.text: The list of this week's bestsellers
choices.why: A few seconds old is fine.

choices.text: An author's biography
Stock that just reached zero
choices.why: Right. It sells a book the shop lacks.

prompt: Fifty readers asked for the stale book. What did they get?

choices.text: The new price, after waiting for the refresh
The old price, at once
An error until the refresh finished
Half old, half new

prompt: How does a reader decide to refresh early under XFetch?

choices.text: It asks the other readers
It refreshes on every read after half the lifetime has gone
By chance, more likely near expiry
A cron job tells it

prompt: Why does XFetch not guarantee exactly one refresh?

choices.text: Redis drops one of the refreshes
beta must be 1
choices.why: beta moves the decision, no more.

choices.text: Each reader rolls independently
It refreshes only quiet keys

prompt: 1,000 keys written at once with a fixed 300-second lifetime. When do they expire?

choices.text: Spread over five minutes
All in the same second
Never, because they were written together
One per second, in order

prompt: With 0 to 60 seconds of jitter, at most how many of the 1,000 keys expired in one second?
One Nginx directive makes concurrent misses for one entry wait for the first: `proxy_cache_lock ___;`.
With `proxy_cache_lock on`, forty visitors asked for one uncached page. What reached the shop?

choices.text: Forty requests, twenty per copy
Nothing; Nginx made the page up
One request
Two requests, one per copy of the shop

prompt: What happens to a request that waits longer than `proxy_cache_lock_timeout`?

choices.text: It gets a 504 Gateway Timeout from Nginx
It goes to the upstream, uncached
It waits forever
choices.why: That is what the timeout prevents.

choices.text: It is served the stale copy

prompt: Match each layer to its answer to the stampede.

pairs.left: Nginx, one miss at a time

prompt: Why does `warm.py` fetch books one at a time?

choices.text: Redis accepts one write at a time
So the database barely notices
Python cannot use threads
Order matters to the cache

prompt: Which is a poor choice of what to warm?

choices.text: The most read pages from the access log
Every item, a million rarely read
The next version's keys before a deploy
The home page

prompt: Put the steps of `lockcache.get_book` on a miss in order, for the reader that wins the lock.
items: Take the lock with NX and PX
Look in the cache once more
Read the database and store the copy
Release the lock if the token matches
trap: Releasing comes last, even on an error.

prompt: Which of these reduce a stampede on one popular key?

choices.text: A lock with a lifetime
Serving stale while one reader refreshes
Probabilistic early refresh
Jitter on the key's lifetime
